title: Metering for server-push partial responses and early push callbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:

We currently meter token usage for two primary interaction models: (1) request/response HTTP batch calls and (2) client-initiated streaming where the client pulls tokens via an open websocket/stream. A growing class of integrations uses server-initiated partial responses (push callbacks, webhooks, or long-lived HTTP/2 server push) where the server delivers intermittent chunks or callbacks that are not strictly tied to a single client-driven request lifecycle. Examples: background async completions sent via webhook, proxying to third-party chat clients that accept server push, and server-initiated partial preview updates for long-running generative jobs.

Problem statement:

These server-push flows introduce metering ambiguity in three ways:
1) Attribution: which request/session should be credited when a push contains both replicated prefix text and new continuation tokens (e.g., resumable jobs resumed by multiple downstream consumers)?
2) Duplication: the same partial response may be pushed to multiple endpoints (fan-out) — we must avoid double-billing while preserving accurate per-customer accounting.
3) Early partial/abort semantics: pushes can be aborted mid-chunk (connection cut by consumer or server cancels). We need deterministic terminal-crediting rules so customers and quotas see consistent usage.

Goal:

Define and implement a deterministic metering protocol and pipeline handling for server-initiated partial responses that: (a) attributes tokens accurately to the originating job/request or customer, (b) deduplicates fan-out pushes to avoid double billing, (c) correctly handles partially-delivered chunks and aborts with clear terminal/partial crediting semantics, and (d) integrates with quota/rate-limiter and billing pipelines with minimal latency impact.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Every server-push chunk must carry a canonical origin token (job_id and origin_customer_id) or be rejected by the ingress layer.
A2: Token attribution must be idempotent: repeated pushes for the same chunk/job within the reconciliation window are not billed multiple times.
A3: When a chunk is partially delivered and then aborted, a deterministic partial-credit rule (rounded token count + partial flag) is emitted and reconciled into customer usage within 5 minutes.
A4: Fan-out to N endpoints must bill only the canonical owner (origin_customer_id) and not downstream recipients unless explicitly configured (e.g., per-recipient billing opt-in).

A5: Integration tests and e2e harness demonstrate billing parity with equivalent client-pull flows for representative workloads (startup: small text previews; steady: high-throughput webhook fan-out).
A6: Monitoring dashboards show 0.1% discrepancy tolerance between emitted meter events and reconciled ledger after rollout for three representative customers (low, medium, high volume).
technical_notes: Ingress contract: extend existing streaming envelope with fields: origin_job_id, origin_customer_id, sequence_number, chunk_hash, terminal_flag. These must be printable ASCII and validated at edge.

Dedupe strategy: two-tier dedupe: (1) upstream idempotency check using chunk_hash and origin_job_id in Redis L1 for hot-path de-dup within 10s; (2) persistent dedupe index in metering datastore (time-partitioned) for final reconciliation up to 7 days.

Partial crediting: compute token count at encoder stage and attach token_count_estimate + partial_byte_count. On abort, emit a "partial_credit" event with rounding rules (ceil(estimated_tokens * delivered_ratio)). Store both estimate and final reconciled count in ledger for audit.
Quota interaction: quota decrement occurs only after idempotency pass and dedupe decision; provisional quota reservations available for long-running jobs using lease tokens to avoid overcommit.
Latency impact: edge validation and L1 dedupe must be sub-millisecond on p99. Use local hot caches partitioned by origin_customer_id shard to avoid cross-tenant contention.
Security: origin_customer_id must be cryptographically signed by the control plane key to prevent forged origin attribution. Verify signature at edge; reject unsigned pushes with 401 and emit alert.
implementation_plan: Design review: finalize envelope contract and signing scheme (2 days). Owner: PM + Security.
Edge change: accept & validate server-push envelope; implement L1 dedupe cache + signature verification (4 days). Owner: edge team.
Metering pipeline: accept partial_credit events and store provisional ledger rows; implement persistent dedupe index (6 days). Owner: billing-engine.
Quota changes: add provisional reservation APIs and lease expirer to avoid double allocation for long-running jobs (3 days). Owner: quota-service.
E2E tests: build harness that simulates fan-out, mid-chunk aborts, and repeated replays (3 days). Owner: SRE + QA.
Canary rollout: enable for internal customers + opt-in customers behind feature flag (2 days). Owner: rollout team.
Full rollout and postmortem: monitor and iterate (ongoing).
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope parsing, signature verification, and chunk_hash generation.
Load test: push 10k/sec partial responses across 100 origin_job_ids with fan-out factor 5; assert L1 dedupe hit rate and p99 latency < 15ms for metering acceptance.
Reconciliation test: replay 1% of messages out-of-order and with duplicates; final ledger must match canonical token counts within 0.01% error after reconciliation run.
Fault injection: simulate abrupt connection closures mid-chunk and verify partial_credit emission and ledger reconciliation.
Integration test against quota service: ensure provisional reservations prevent quota exhaustion race between two concurrent push producers.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy edge and billing pipeline changes behind feature flag for internal tenant (redwood-internal). Phase 2: Enable for 3 opt-in customers with monitoring + dedicated billing reconciliation. Phase 3: Broad enablement with runtime-1.22 release. Each phase lasts minimum 48 hours of traffic verification; auto-rollback threshold: >0.5% unexplained billing delta or any quota overdraws.
monitoring: Metric: push_ingest_accept_rate by origin_customer_id and origin_job_type.
Alert: unexplained_billing_delta > 0.5% over 1h for canary customers.
Dashboard: partial_vs_final_token_ratio (time series) and per-customer reconciliation lag (p50/p95).
comments: 2026-02-10 Maya Chen: Created ticket after field report from SRE about webhook billing disputes. Initial scope drafted.

2026-02-17 Aarav Patel: Design sync held. Decided on two-tier dedupe and cryptographic signing to prevent forgery. Action: edge prototype and signing scheme doc (link: https://drive.redwood.internal/md/push-signing).

2026-02-23 Priya Nambiar (Billing): Raised concern about long reconciliation windows for partially-delivered chunks causing invoice drift. Suggested storing both estimated and reconciled token counts and surfacing them in invoices. Marked for acceptance criteria A3.

2026-03-02 SRE: Load test run completed; L1 dedupe reduces duplicate billing by ~98% in simulated fan-out. Two issues found related to Redis hot-shard contention; added shard-smoothing task to implementation plan.
2026-03-08 QA: E2E harness ready. Found edge case where unsigned pushes were accepted by an older proxy; added explicit rejection and compatibility test.
2026-03-10 Aarav Patel: Updated estimate to 5 points after design refinements; moving to Planned.
